fact_check_verdict: PASS on primary doc (all 12 pages read) plus LawSites corroboration of core rules. CourtSmart item is single-source and forward-looking. Doc is hosted by LawNext, attribute as a copy of the policy published by LawSites. No claim about whether transcripts are live. Nothing about judges remaining responsible. AVA chatbot not tied to the policy.

claims.spoken: A policy written for Alaska's court staff and judges says how they may use artificial intelligence.
requires: p1; copy published by LawSites. Never say it was issued today.

claims.spoken: It's version one point two, dated June.
requires: Cover: Version 1.2 June 2026. Internal doc, no public release date.

claims.spoken: It applies to every court employee and every judge.
requires: p3: all court staff and judicial officers.

claims.spoken: It allows A I, if people check every answer.
requires: p3: must review and verify all outputs before you use it.

claims.spoken: Staff must check legal citations and verify factual claims.
requires: p5 Rule 5.

claims.spoken: For legal research, only A I trained on legal authorities should be used.
requires: p3: SHOULD be used, not must.

claims.spoken: The court names Westlaw Precision as a tool it has.
Staff must never type confidential or personal information into an A I tool.
requires: p4 Rule 2.

claims.spoken: Personal A I accounts can't be used for work.
requires: p6 Rule 8.

claims.spoken: Staff can't download A I programs onto court devices.
claims.on_screen: NO AI DOWNLOADS ON COURT DEVICES
requires: p6 Rule 9. Court-owned devices only.

claims.spoken: Staff and judges may not use A I on their own to make notes or transcripts of hearings.
requires: p6 Rule 10 verbatim: You may not independently use AI and GenAI to generate notes or transcripts of live or recorded court hearings.

claims.spoken: The example is a clerk using Zoom's A I transcription for a log note.
requires: p6. The example names court clerks; the ban covers all covered users.

claims.spoken: A I assistants that join a hearing should be removed.
requires: p7 Rule 11: SHOULD be removed.

claims.spoken: But the court says its own staff and judges will soon get A I transcripts of all hearings.
requires: p6: will soon have access to transcripts for all court hearings.

claims.spoken: Those transcripts come automatically from CourtSmart, the court's recording system.
requires: p6: generated automatically by CourtSmart as part of our court recording system.

claims.spoken: The policy says they should be ready by fall.
requires: p6: should be available by fall 2026. Plan, not a guarantee. Live status UNVERIFIED, never say they are live or launched.

claims.spoken: The policy calls them A I generated and not the official court record.
requires: p6 verbatim: These transcripts are AI generated and are not the official court record.

claims.spoken: They will link to the official audio.
requires: p6: useful links to the official audio record for review.

claims.spoken: They are restricted to internal court use and may not be shared with the public.
claims.on_screen: INTERNAL ONLY · NOT FOR THE PUBLIC
requires: p6 verbatim: restricted to internal ACS use and may not be shared with the public.

claims.spoken: The policy's reason is that hearings may hold confidential information that couldn't be removed from the A I system, even if a hearing was later sealed.
claims.on_screen: SEALED LATER? CAN'T BE PULLED BACK
requires: p6 verbatim: Hearings may contain confidential or personal information that could not be removed from the AI system even if a party objected or a hearing was later sealed.

claims.spoken: Parties can ask for the official audio with form T F three oh four.
requires: p7: Parties may use form TF-304 to request official audio recordings.

claims.spoken: Version one point two adds mandatory training and a signed form.
requires: p7 Rule 14; new to v1.2.

claims.spoken: Current staff get ninety days. New hires get thirty.
requires: p7. Do not compute a calendar deadline.

claims.spoken: A I written code must be reviewed and tested by a human.
requires: p7 Rule 12.

claims.spoken: A I must not be used to interpret court proceedings.
Violations can bring discipline, up to firing.
requires: p12: up to and including dismissal.

claims.spoken: A national survey of judicial A I policies, published November fifth, lists Alaska as having a policy.
requires: LawSites (Bob Ambrogi) Nov 5 2026; Alaska status Policy v1.2. Survey does not mention CourtSmart.

claims.spoken: The policy itself says the court asked an A I tool to help format an early draft of it.
requires: p9-10: court prompted a GenAI tool with a draft of this policy to improve formatting. Formatting only.

claims.spoken: The transcripts are live.
requires: CUT. No source says CourtSmart AI transcripts are live or delayed. Say only expected by fall.
